note: Chapter 5 dialogue, The Meridian Line (Willow Bend, Kessler's Tank, the westbound express, Halvorsen Ranch). Original writing.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Thursday's westbound express carries the syndicate payroll for the whole Sable country. And in the express safe, Pell's own ledger. He won't trust it to a bank, not after the Exchange.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Eleven thousand dollars and the only book in the territory worth reading. Christmas has come on a Thursday.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: That's how they did it to Tom. A Thursday train, a safe, a messenger in the door. I heard you tell it, Ruth. More than once.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I know how they did it, Hap. I've had eighteen months to learn it by heart.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: The grade below Kessler's Tank slows them to a walk for water. If you wanted to do it Tom's way, that's where you'd do it.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I'd like it noted that the doctor was consulted and called this a terrible idea. Then I'd like it noted that I'm coming.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I can uncouple a car. I watched a brakeman do it at Bitter Spring. Twice. He swore the whole time, so I know the words too.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: The ledger. Nobody fires first. Nobody puts a gun on the messenger unless he puts one on us.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Then I'll hold the horses. Somebody steady ought to, and I'm the steadiest thing in camp. Mostly from the stitches.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: A train robbery where we leave the money. The Arceneaux name has never been so embarrassed.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: All of it. The payroll was bought with stolen land. We're only taking it back the long way round.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Then I won't come. I won't hold horses while you do to some messenger's wife what was done to you. I'll keep the camp. Somebody should.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Now that's a sentence I've waited my whole life to hear from an honest woman.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I'll ride Thursday. After that I'll think about whose fight this is.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: There. The tank, the grade, the cut. They take water here and climb out slow. A good horse can run alongside for half a mile.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Harlan's Siding had a tank like this one. Tom used to wave to the boys filling it. He waved at everybody.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Then we'll wave too. From closer than they'd like.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Thursday, then. A rag on the third pole past the tank. When the engine passes it, we go.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Ruth? Is this what they did? To your husband?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Close enough to make me sick, Billy. Go and feed the horses.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Smoke on the east grade. She's on time. Pell's trains always are.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Billy and I take the engine. You take the express car. Try not to fall under it; it would spoil my afternoon.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: She's slowing! She's slowing for the tank! Go, Ruth, go!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Del! Stop the engine!

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: The engineer's very obliging. I told him I'm from New Orleans. People will believe anything about New Orleans.

lines.speaker: guard
lines.line: Wells and Merriweather! Back away from the car or be carried away from it!

lines.speaker: harmon
lines.line: I've a shotgun and a wife in Port Linden, lady. I'd as soon keep both.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Put the gun down and you'll keep the both of them. I swear it on a man who stood where you're standing.

lines.speaker: harmon
lines.line: They all say that. The ones who robbed the Harlan's Siding car said it, I heard. Then they shot the messenger anyway.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: His name was Tom Caddell. He was my husband. I'm not them. Open the safe and go home to your wife.

lines.speaker: harmon
lines.line: Caddell. I knew Tom. We drank at the depot in Topeka, him and me. All right. All right, God help me.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Ruth. Ruth, what did you do? He was putting it down.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Was he? I couldn't tell. I couldn't tell any more.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: There's a book in here! A big one, with a lock on it like a church Bible!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That's the one. Leave the rest where it lies.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: And the rest of it in canvas sacks, very orderly. Mr. Pell likes his robberies tidy.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Riders out of the caboose! They had men aboard! They knew!

lines.speaker: ashby
lines.line: Caddell! Mr. Pell sends his compliments! He's been expecting you since Tuesday!

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Ruth! The horses! I'm hit, God help me, I'm hit!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hap! Hold on! Joseph, get him up!

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Get him across a saddle! Ride for Halvorsen's! Ride!

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: They knew. Somebody told Pell we were coming.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Pell didn't need telling. He reads the same newspapers we do.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Wells and Merriweather. Tom's company. Of course it is.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: The ball's under his ribs. I need light, boiling water, and nobody talking to me unless it's useful.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Use the kitchen table. I'll boil the water. I've boiled water for worse men than Hap Lindqvist.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: It's out. He'll live, if he can be persuaded to lie still for a month, which he can't.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Did we get the book, at least? I'd hate to be shot for nothing. It's bad for a man's dignity.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Ruth. He went quietly, which is more than I'd have managed.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Tell the boy... tell him the stew's in the pot. He'll know what I mean.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: The camp's burning! Hap! Hap!

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: The posse came through at noon, the tracks say. Six riders. He made them pay for it. There are two of them in the creek.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He said somebody should keep the camp.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: He kept it. Lord, he kept it.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: He used to hum when he cooked. Three hymns at once. I don't know any of them right.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then hum them wrong. He'd like that better.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: So. Eleven thousand dollars on Ingrid's table, or a book with a lock on it. What are we, Ruth?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: That's the question. It's been the question since Bitter Spring.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Fenn gets the ledger. The payroll goes back to the ranches and the camps it was squeezed out of. Every dollar.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Then I'll take my share of nothing and go, cher. I told you I'd bring my own deck. I never said I'd stay at the table.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Then I'll stay a while longer. It seems to be my fight after all.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: We keep it. We've been shot at, burned out and buried for it. It's ours.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Then it isn't mine. I've seen where this road goes, Ruth. I won't stand and watch you walk it.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: I'll stay. Somebody has to count it, and I don't trust Doc's arithmetic.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: My arithmetic is excellent. It's my judgement that's in question, and I'm still here.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Tom's watch says ten past four. It's said ten past four for eighteen months. I keep winding it anyway.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You shot a messenger in the door of his car, Ruth. I can't ride with that. I'm sorry. I truly am.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Whatever you decide, decide it outside my kitchen. I've only just scrubbed the table.
